q: 1. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: The completion point of an activity is called an event, represented as a node/connector point - all the above terms apply.

q: 2. Variance is
options: (Sum of time duration for various job) / number of jobs
difference between time under consideration and mean time
mean of square root of mean of squared deviation
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: Per the answer key, c. Standard theory defines variance as the mean of squared deviations, so the key and options look garbled.

q: 3. If for a activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: The most likely time is cut off in the scan. The key answer 3.5 follows from tE = (1 + 4m + 8)/6 with m = 3 days.

q: 4. Standard deviation when optimistic time and earliest expected time
explain: The stem is incomplete in the book. Using the previous question's data, σ = (8 – 1)/6 = 1.167 days.

q: 5. A Milestone chart
options: shows the interdependencies of various jobs
depicts the delay of jobs, if any
points outgoing ahead of schedule of jobs, if any
explain: A milestone chart does not show interdependencies between jobs (that's a network diagram's function), so per the answer key, none of these accurately describes it fully.

q: 6. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: Combining decreasing indirect costs and increasing direct costs yields a distinct U-shaped total cost curve with a clear minimum cost point.

q: 7. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: in a network activities are represented by arrows and events are circled
events into which a number of activities enter and from which one or several activities emerge are called the merge nodes
events into which one or several activities enter and from which a number of emerging activities are generated are called burst nodes
explain: All three statements are correct, so d.

q: 8. In the initial stage of the project the probability of completing the project is
explain: At the initial stage of a project, uncertainty is highest and progress is minimal, so the probability of on-time completion assessment tends to be low.

q: 9. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float = total float – free float.

q: 10. Negative float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Negative float means super-critical.

q: 11. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or replanning is called
explain: Updating is the process of incorporating changes and rescheduling/replanning the project based on actual progress.

q: 12. Zero float any activity means that the activity is
explain: Zero float means critical.

q: 13. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Positive float means sub-critical.

q: 14. The total float for any activity along the critical path in CPM is
explain: Critical activities have zero total float.

q: 15. Choose the correct statement from the following:
explain: PERT is indeed event-oriented, making this the correct statement among the options.

q: 16. Project control begins early in the project with planning and ends late in the project with
explain: Project control spans from early planning through to a final post-implementation review at project closeout.

q: 17. Identify the man out
explain: 'Design completed' is an event; the others are activities.

q: 18. An important principle in drawing a network is
options: no activity can start until all the previous activities in the same chain are completed
parallel activities should begin and end at the same time
between two events there should not be more than two activities
the number of dummy activities in a network should not exceed 4
has no bearing on the network and appear anywhere
explain: The precedence rule: an activity starts only after all its predecessors finish.

q: 19. If the scheduled completion time of a project is more than the earliest expected time for completion of the project, then the probability of completion of the project within the scheduled completion time will be
explain: If the scheduled time exceeds the expected (mean) time, the project has a higher-than-average chance of completion within schedule, i.e., more than 50%.

q: 20. A dummy activity
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: A dummy consumes no time or resources.

q: 21. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges, it results in an error called
explain: An event with no outgoing activity is a dangling error.

q: 22. Aggregate planning is planning for
explain: Aggregate planning looks at the total capacity and resource needs for the entire project rather than individual small tasks.

q: 23. Critical path moves along the activities having total float?
explain: By definition, the critical path consists of activities with zero total float.

q: 24. Negative slack occurs
options: when lastest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events sticks to their schedule
explain: Per the answer key, c. Negative slack arises when the schedule is behind, which needs extra resources.

q: 25. Critical path
explain: The critical path has the minimum slack (zero or negative).

q: 26. The objective of technical planning is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
taking remedial action about bottle-neck in execution
explain: Technical planning covers the entire lifecycle from setting standards to resource management and problem-solving during execution.

q: 27. For the execution of work in time, work plan is prepared by
explain: The contractor is responsible for creating the detailed schedule and work plan to ensure they meet the contractual deadlines.

q: 28. Crashing is
explain: Crashing reduces duration.

q: 29. Which one is the basis of project?
explain: A project is built on the pillars of planning what to do, scheduling when to do it, and monitoring to ensure it is done correctly.

q: 30. In PERT (Programme Evaluation & Review Technique) analysis the duration of the activities is taken as:
explain: PERT uses the expected mean time (calculated from the three time estimates) as the duration for scheduling calculations.

q: 31. Latest starts of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event tie of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: Per the answer key, a.

q: 32. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: Waiting takes time, so it is an activity.

q: 33. An activity of the project is graphically represented by ……… on the network.
explain: Activities are arrows; events are circles.

q: 34. Which of the following statement is correct about the network diagram?
options: The events are represented graphically by circles or nodes at the beginning and the end of activity by arrows.
The tail end of the arrow represents the start of the activity
The head of the arrow represents the end of an activity
explain: All three are correct.

q: 35. Which operation must complete first?
options: Right of the line joining two circles
Left of the line joining two circle
explain: The operation on the left (the predecessor) completes first.

q: 36. Critical path method (CPM) requires:
explain: CPM uses a single deterministic time estimate for each activity, unlike PERT's three estimates.

q: 37. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be
explain: An operation can have one or more predecessors.

q: 38. The post-operations in CPM are marked
explain: Successors are marked to the right.

q: 39. In CPM method, the earliest finish is indicated by time on
options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: Per the answer key, in a rectangle at the top right, outside the circle.

q: 40. CPM stand for:
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method.

q: 41. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by a
explain: Per the answer key, a triangle.

q: 42. A bar chart is drawn for:
explain: A bar chart plots time against activities, with bar length representing each activity's duration.

q: 43. Dummy activities are used to
explain: Dummies maintain the required logic of the network.

q: 44. Which of the following are the guidelines for the construction of a network diagram?
options: Each activity is represented by one only arrow in the network
Dangling must be avoided in a network diagram
Dummy activity consumes no time or resource
explain: All three are network-construction guidelines.

q: 45. A CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is differences in the planned and actual performance
explain: Network updating is done whenever a deviation is found between planned and actual performance, requiring revision.

q: 46. In PERT, optimistic time represents the following time taken by an activity.
options: expected or average time taken when the activity is repeated several times
time taken if there is delay at every stage except due to natural calamities
minimum possible time taken under ideal conditions
most likely time taken under normal conditions
explain: Optimistic time represents the minimum possible duration an activity would take assuming everything goes ideally well.

q: 47. PERT stands for
options: Pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Programme Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 48. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: Completion of an activity is marked by an event, represented as a node/connector point - all of above apply.

q: 49. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and time required to complete the activity
explain: Float can be equivalently expressed via any of these differences (LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or available-required time) - all of the above are valid definitions.

q: 50. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents:
explain: The critical path represents the minimum time required to complete the entire project.
